subject: Re: Acero Labs — competitive replacement economics & credits
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acero.com>, Raj Patel <raj@acero.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring replacement economics — Redwood vs AtlasML

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re evaluating a potential replacement of our incumbent vendor (AtlasML) and need a clear view of the near-term economics to present to procurement and the CFO. High level asks:

- A line-item comparison (per-token, embeddings, orchestration fees) for matched feature parity.
- Any one-time migration credit or onboarding discount you can offer to offset egress/onboarding costs.
- Clarify packaging options: seat-based vs usage-only vs committed throughput, and what typical customers our size choose.
- Any performance rebates or SLA credits you can commit to for a first-year pilot.

Attached is our anonymized usage export (acero_usage_profile.csv). We expect a 3–6 month pilot at ~1B tokens/month with 100k embeddings/month and spiky inference patterns during peak hours.

Timeline: procurement wants an economics summary and proposed credit by end of week (3/18) to include in the vendor comparison.

Can you put something together? If you prefer a sync, happy to schedule.

—Marta
Procurement Manager, Acero Labs
[Attachment: acero_usage_profile.csv (text/csv)]

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics — Redwood vs AtlasML

Marta —

Thanks for the usage export and context. We can absolutely put together a line-item comparison and a limited-time migration package. Before I draft specifics, two quick clarifying questions so we align the proposal:

1) For the pilot you mentioned, do you expect production traffic to run on Redwood (served traffic) or a mixed run with AtlasML during the migration window?
2) Can you confirm the average sequence length and percent of requests that require function/tool-calling or streaming (that changes token burn assumptions)?

Ben and Marcus are looped in — Ben will validate the performance math; Marcus will propose an economic structure (credits, rebates).

I can get a first-draft counterproposal to you by EOD Wednesday (3/16) if the answers above are quick. If procurement prefers a short live session to walk the spreadsheet, I can make time tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[redwood.com]

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics — Redwood vs AtlasML

Marta / Olga —

Quick tech note on the usage file you shared:

- Avg. sequence length looks ~120 tokens; 99th percentile bursts reach ~1.1k tokens (these drive GPU mem/slots).
- ~18% of calls use tool-calling/structured output; streaming is negligible today.
- With continuous batching and prefix caching we estimate ~18–25% per-token cost reduction vs unoptimized runs on AtlasML hardware for similar model families.

Implications: migration credits should focus on peak-window concurrency and cold-start KV cache (those are the main ephemeral infra egress costs).

I’ll attach a migration credit sketch and a preliminary per-token/embedding mapping given the numbers.

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: migration_credit_breakdown.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed structure — tiered commit + surge credits

Marta —

Per our review, we can present two viable commercial structures for Acero’s pilot and potential full migration:

Option A — Commit + Tiered Volume Discount (recommended for predictability)
- 12-mo commit: $0.0023 per token active generation, $0.00045 per embedding.
- 15% volume discount applied monthly once commit thresholds exceeded.
- Migration credit: $50,000 applied against first-month invoice.
- Onboarding support: 2 weeks professional services included.

Option B — Usage-first + Surge Credits (recommended if you expect spike variability)
- No long-term commit: $0.0026 per token, $0.00055 per embedding.
- Surge credit pool: $75,000 one-time credit usable within first 90 days for excess peak spend.
- Performance rebate: if we meet 99th percentile latency SLA <120ms for pilot, rebate of 5% of pilot spend (paid as credit).

Conditions: credits are contingent on a 90-day pilot with standard onboarding milestones and an agreed rollback plan. We can provide a DocuSign with the counters once terms are agreed.

I’m attaching a concise redwood_counterproposal_mar2027.pdf with line items and a recommended timeline (pilot start target: early April).

—Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_counterproposal_mar2027.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acero.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acero.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed structure — tiered commit + surge credits

Thanks Marcus, Ben, Olga —

Appreciate the two structures. A few follow-ups from procurement/CFO:

1) The CFO asked whether the $75k surge credit could be elevated to a $100k migration credit if we commit to a 6–9 month renewal post-pilot. If you can, that materially changes the financial calculus.
2) We need to see the proposed DocuSign terms (term sheet + standard SOW). Can you also include the SLA language for performance rebate triggers?
3) Any flexibility on invoicing cadence — CFO prefers monthly invoices net 30, but will consider quarterly in arrears if there is a prepay discount.
4) Security/compliance quick ask: do you have SOC 2 Type II scope and can you confirm data residency options in US regions?

If possible, can you update the counterproposal with the $100k migration credit option as a conditional line item? Procurement will use that in the internal vendor scorecard.

—Marta
Procurement Manager, Acero Labs

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acero.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed structure — tiered commit + surge credits

Marta —

Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a $100k migration credit with a conditional 6–9 month renewal commitment. Outline below (we’ll put formal language in the DocuSign):

Final conditional offer (summary):
- Pilot: 90 days; target start early April.
- Migration credit: $100,000 one-time credit applied to first three invoices if Acero signs a 6-month or 9-month renewal (pre-agreed tiers) within 30 days after the pilot close.
- Pricing: Option B baseline (usage-first) at $0.0026/token and $0.00055/embedding for pilot.
- Volume discount: 10% off token rates for the 12 months following a signed renewal.
- Performance rebate: 5% credit on pilot spend if we meet the agreed latency SLA (99th < 120ms) and error rate <0.2%.
- Onboarding: priority migration queue + 3 days of remote engineering time included.
- Invoicing: monthly net 30 by default; we can offer quarterly in arrears with a 2% prepay discount if Acero elects a 12-month prepayment.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II (in-scope), US-region residency available (AWS us-east-1 or us-west-2).

Next steps: I’ll send an updated redwood counterproposal pdf and a DocuSign with the conditional migration credit language. If that looks good, Raj or procurement can sign the DocuSign and we’ll schedule the onboarding kickoff.

Attaching: redwood_counterproposal_mar2027.pdf (updated) and migration_credit_breakdown.xlsx as requested.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_counterproposal_mar2027.pdf (application/pdf)]
